title: Geo-affinity latency orchestrator: blended p50/p95 + network-health routing policy
creator: Evelyn Hart
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a 'Geo-affinity Latency Orchestrator' routing policy which selects regional POPs and capacity tiers by combining short- and long-tail latency percentiles (p50 and p95) with a normalized network health score. The goal is to reduce end-user tail-latency regressions while keeping regional affinity (reduce cross-region egress) and gracefully falling back to compatible model variants when primary variants or regions degrade.

Background and motivation:
Current region selector uses simple p50 heuristics and an availability flag. We observe cases where p50 is good but p95 spikes intermittently causing customer-visible tails. We also see network-level degradation (packet loss, high retransmit rates) that correlate with increased upstream SLO violations. A blended policy will avoid oscillation and keep traffic on affinity POPs when appropriate while failing over predictably when tail-latency or net-health exceed thresholds.

Core proposal:
1) Telemetry inputs: rolling-window p50 and p95 per region per model-variant, and a network health score (0-1) computed from network metrics (loss, jitter, tcp-retransmits, average RTT to backend).
2) Scoring function: compute normalized latency metrics (0 best, 1 worst) then form score = alpha * norm_p95 + beta * norm_p50 + gamma * (1 - net_health) + delta * recent_error_rate_penalty. Tunable weights (alpha >= beta, alpha+beta+gamma+delta = 1). Default weights: alpha=0.55, beta=0.25, gamma=0.15, delta=0.05.
3) Smoothing & stability: apply exponential decay to percentiles (tau = 5m) and enforce a min decision window (60s) and regional hysteresis (cooldown) to prevent flapping.
4) Tier-aware routing: prefer same-tier capacity first (dedicated > hosted-burst > hosted) and apply a tier-penalty to score when crossing tiers to avoid unnecessary cross-tier routing.
5) Variant fallback: maintain a compatibility matrix of model variants; when primary variant in a region is degraded, pick the highest-ranked compatible variant in the same region before routing cross-region.
6) Circuit-breaker: if score > fail_threshold (default 0.8) for sustained duration (2min), mark region+variant as degraded and shift traffic using the weighted scores.

Success criteria:
- Reduce end-user tail latency p95 by >= 10% for test traffic compared to baseline policy on same test week.
- No increase in cross-region egress above 5% of baseline for affinity-bound workloads.
- No material increase in error-rates due to route changes during rollout.

Notes on integration:
- This policy plugs into SmartRouter decision layer; requires new scoring API to accept blended telemetry and return a ranked list of region+variant targets with weights.
- Telemetry pipeline must provide per-region p50/p95 with 1m resolution and a derived network health score (see telemetry_queries below).
- Console needs small UX addition: per-route "routing-score" time series and feature flags to enable sticky vs. aggressive fallback.
acceptance_criteria: New routing policy implemented and exposed via SmartRouter API that returns ranked region+variant+weight
Telemetry feeds (p50/p95 and network health) consumed with <=30s ingestion lag in staging
Unit + integration tests covering scoring, hysteresis, and circuit-breaker behavior
Canary rollout automation: 10% traffic for 12h, monitor p95 and errors, then 50% then 100%
Console dashboard showing per-region blended score and decision audit logs

telemetry_queries: p50/p95 query: SELECT region, model_variant, percentile_cont(0.5) as p50, percentile_cont(0.95) as p95 FROM request_latency WHERE ts > now() - interval '5 minutes' GROUP BY region, model_variant
network health: compute normalized score = 1 - clamp(0,1,(0.6*loss + 0.3*jitter_norm + 0.1*retransmit_rate)) from net_telemetry
error rate penalty: recent_error_rate = errors_last_2m / requests_last_2m
rollout_plan: Deploy scoring service to staging and run synthetic benchmark across 6 POPs
Canary 1: route 5-10% of real traffic (low-risk customers) for 12 hours, monitor p95, error-rate, cross-region egress
Canary 2: 50% traffic for 24 hours if canary1 is clean
Full rollout: 100% after 72h clean telemetry or manual rollback
Fallback: feature-flag to revert to legacy p50-only selector instantly
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring math with deterministic inputs
Integration test that injects synthetic p95 spikes and verifies routing shifts to local compatible variants
Chaos test: network loss injection in one POP to validate circuit-breaker and cooldown
Load test: ensure scoring service adds <2ms decision latency at 10k RPS
comments: 2025-11-12 - Evelyn Hart: Created ticket. Initial proposal drafted after sync with product. Goal: add p95 sensitivity and network health into region selection without causing cross-region thrash.

2025-11-14 - Marco Ruiz: Prototype scoring function implemented in local branch. Using default weights alpha=0.55/beta=0.25/gamma=0.15/delta=0.05. Early results on synthetic traces look promising (p95 down ~12%).
2025-11-17 - Gabe Lin: Telemetry prework done. Updated Kafka topic to include per-pop retransmit_rate. Need agreement on net_health formula; added query draft in telemetry_queries.

2025-11-19 - Priya Menon: Added hysteresis and cooldown design. Suggested 60s min-window + 5m exponential smoothing to avoid reacting to microbursts. Also recommended coarse-grained change logs for observability.

2025-11-21 - Sumi Patel: Compatibility matrix schema proposed. Will store as a small indexed table (region, primary_variant, compatible_variants[], last_validated_ts). Need migration story for existing variants.
2025-11-24 - Alice Cho (Design): Console mockups uploaded. UX shows blended score time-series and a toggle to prefer 'affinity-preserving' vs 'latency-first' behavior per-route.
